extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent practitioners, and public stakeholders (commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applying 35 U.S.C. 101 to determine patent-eligible subject matter; intended primarily for USPTO examiners but also published for public comment and practitioner use. The July 2015 Update supplements the 2014 Interim Patent Eligibility Guidance with examples, discussion, and case references.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2014 Interim Patent Eligibility Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance prepared for use by USPTO personnel in determining subject matter eligibility under 35 U.S.C. 101 (published in the Federal Register on December 16, 2014).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the baseline test/approach for examiners to determine subject matter eligibility; the 2014 Interim Guidance was the document on which public comment was solicited and which the July 2015 Update is intended to assist in applying during patent examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: July 2015 Update: Subject Matter Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An update produced in response to public comments on the 2014 Interim Patent Eligibility Guidance, intended to assist examiners in applying that guidance during the patent examination process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes new examples and discussion of issues raised by public comments; the USPTO is seeking public comment on the July 2015 Update. Examiners are directed to use the Update with the 2014 Interim Guidance when making eligibility determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for additional examples (particularly for claims directed to abstract ideas and laws of nature)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Public comment theme) Requests for additional examples, particularly for claims directed to abstract ideas and laws of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Update adds new illustrative examples (see Appendix 1) to clarify how the guidance applies to claims that may be directed to abstract ideas or laws of nature; examples are intended to show application of the eligibility framework and to help examiners identify ineligible subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further explanation of the "markedly different characteristics" analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: (Public comment theme) Requests for further explanation of the markedly different characteristics analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Update responds with additional discussion and examples addressing how to analyze whether claimed subject matter possesses markedly different characteristics from a judicial exception (e.g., laws of nature, natural phenomena, abstract ideas), informing examiner determinations under the eligibility framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: How examiners identify abstract ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: (Public comment theme) Requests for further information regarding how examiners identify abstract ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Update provides additional guidance and illustrative claim examples to clarify what constitutes an abstract idea and how examiners should recognize abstract-idea-type judicial exceptions in claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prima facie case and the role of evidence with respect to eligibility rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: (Public comment theme) Discussion of the prima facie case and the role of evidence with respect to eligibility rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Update discusses the establishment of a prima facie case for an eligibility rejection and the evidentiary role (and limits) of evidence in the eligibility context, clarifying how examiners should support eligibility rejections and consider applicant responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of the 2014 Interim Patent Eligibility Guidance in the Patent Examining Corps
rubrics_metrics.description: (Public comment theme) Requests for information regarding application of the 2014 Interim Patent Eligibility Guidance in the Patent Examining Corps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Update explains how the guidance should be applied in practice within the Patent Examining Corps, aiming to promote consistent application across examiners and art units and to address implementation concerns raised in public comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of preemption in the eligibility analysis (including streamlined analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Public comment theme) Explanation of the role of preemption in the eligibility analysis, including a discussion of the streamlined analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Update includes discussion on how consideration of preemption informs the eligibility inquiry and explains the streamlined analysis (when and how it may be applied) so examiners can consider whether a claim improperly monopolizes a judicial exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix 1: New illustrative examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix 1 provides new examples illustrative of major themes from the public comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These example claim sets are intended to show concrete application of the eligibility framework (including analyses of abstract ideas, laws of nature, markedly different characteristics, and preemption) to help examiners and practitioners understand likely outcomes and reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix 2: Comprehensive index of examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix 2 is a comprehensive index of examples for use with the 2014 Interim Patent Eligibility Guidance, including new and previously issued examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a referenceable collection of example analyses to assist examiners in locating precedent examples and analogies when evaluating particular claim types under the guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix 3: Selected eligibility cases discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix 3 lists and discusses selected eligibility cases from the Supreme Court and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarizes and discusses key judicial decisions relevant to subject matter eligibility to ground examiner application of the guidance in controlling and persuasive case law; intended to assist understanding of legal background and reasoning.
